To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Bipolar disorder and borderline personality disorder are associated with differential patterns of functional network connectivity (Fnc); 2) Bipolar disorder was associated with increased Fnc while borderline personality disorder was associated with decreased Fnc; 3) Impaired Fnc was associated with impulsivity in borderline personality disorder and emotional clarity and awareness in bipolar disorder.

Bipolar and borderline patients show differential patterns of functional network connectivity during resting state, which may help differentiate the disorders and provide insight into the underlying neurobiology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of emotion regulation and social cognition.
the neurobiology of affective and personality disorders and the development of novel treatments.
the neural mechanisms underpining emotional and interpersonal functioning in BD and BPD.

the neural mechanisms of BD and BDP are not only different but that the differences are not limited to a single network.
the FNC approach has the potential to provide an objective biomarker to differentiate between BD and BPD, which may have implications for clinical practice.
the neural mechanisms underlying overlapping symptoms of BD and BDP are different.

there are differential neural mechanisms that give rise to the overlapping clinical symptoms in BD and BPD.
